predecessors.name: County of Flanders
predecessors.text: the Boulonnais, inside the Flanders shape in 1187

successors.name: Royal domain of France
successors.text: the county of Boulogne, exchanged with Louis XI in 1477

ledger.x: 1188: Cliopatria's County of Boulogne row begins; the page is silent on a founding.
1190: Renaud of Dammartin becomes Count of Boulogne.
1212: Philip II takes the county into the royal hands.
1214: after Bouvines the county goes to the king's son Philip Hurepel.
1223: 'Boulogne passed under nominal royal control in 1223', when 'Philip Hurepel became count jure uxoris upon his marriage to Matilda II' (Renaud's daughter).
1238: Matilda II marries Alphonse, second son of Alfonso II of Portugal (king as Afonso III from 1248; he divorced her in 1253).
1259: the county passes to the Counts of Auvergne.
1437: 'Bertrand V de la Tour succeeded to the counties of Auvergne and of Boulogne in 1437.'
1477: the county is incorporated into the royal domain.

wars.name: Battle of Bouvines
wars.outcome: Renaud of Dammartin, Count of Boulogne, fought on the imperial side, was defeated by Philip II and held at Péronne until his death (1227); his county was granted to Philip Hurepel.

wars.name: War of the Burgundian Succession
wars.outcome: French forces seized Artois, Boulogne, Ponthieu and Vermandois in the first months of 1477; the County page has Bertrand II exchange Boulogne with Louis XI the same year.

certainty.note: A small fief with no boundary on any page; the outline is Cliopatria's two-cell shape.
